vs. 
Jamuna Knitting and Dyeing Ltd & others ----- Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment: 37. In this connection it may further be mentioned that admittedly plaintiff No. 1 is a company and plaintiff No. 2 is the Managing Director of that company. If a company wants to pre-empt a land as contiguous land owner, it is incumbent upon the company to show that they are authorised to exercise that right by the Memorandum of Association of the company. A company cannot do a thing unless it is authorised to do so i.e. unless that power has been given to the company by the Memorandum of Association. The Memorandum of Association has not been produced before the Court nor any Board resolution has been produced to show that the company has ever decided to buy the suit land. Besides, there is also no resolution showing that the plaintiff No. 2 has been authorised to file the case on behalf of the company as well. The plaintiff No. 1 is not a natural person and it acts through its Board of Directors. If the company wants to buy any land it must so decide in a Board meeting. No resolution of such Board meeting has been produced. It is also not averred in the plaint that the Board in its meeting decided to buy the suit land. These are the requirements of law. There is no averment in the plaint nor there is any evidence adduced that the plaintiff No. 1 had ever decided to go for pre-empting the suit land as contiguous land holder. Besides, it is neither averred nor proved by any oral or documentary evidence that PW 1 as Managing Director of plaintiff No. 1 was authorised to exercise such authority on behalf of the company. Withholding of the Memorandum of Association and the non-production of any Board resolution showing that the plaintiff No. 1 company has decided to file the instant suit speaks volumes against the plaintiffs. Thus, the suit so far it relates to plaintiff No. 1 is also not maintainable on this count. In this connection it may also be mentioned that with- holding the impartial witness who admittedly accompanied. PW 1 on 9-3-1997 and 19-3-1997 also speaks volumes against the plaintiffs and it appears to us to be a fit case where adverse presumption can be drawn that if any of the neutral persons would have been examined they would not support the case of the plaintiffs.
